title: The Verdict of Bellwether Lane
premise: When a drowned man washes up on the tidal flats below Bellwether Lane wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, insurance investigator Elodie Amberdale discovers the dead man was the beneficiary of a policy she once helped deny — and that the sole witness to the drowning, a woman named Maren Quill, is officially recorded as dead. Elodie's investigation unravels a decades-old inheritance scheme in the village of Saltmere, where the founding family faked a death to protect an heir and let an innocent man hang for a murder he didn't commit. As the tide erodes the evidence, Elodie must choose between closing the case cleanly and exposing a witness whose survival depends on remaining dead. In the end, Elodie finds Maren alive, hidden in the salt marshes, and forces Saltmere to trade its buried inheritance for the truth — paying the price of survival in confessions rather than blood.
about_author: Zephyrine Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating deaths along the English coast before turning to fiction. She writes in a converted pilot's cottage, where the tide chart on her kitchen wall is said to be more accurate than the one published by the admiralty.

chapters.title: The Clothes Make the Corpse
chapters.summary: Elodie Amberdale is called to the tidal flats at Saltmere, where a drowned man wears garments lifted from her own hotel closet — down to the monogrammed cufflinks she never bought. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: professional composure cracking into unease as the crime scene becomes personal.

chapters.title: A Policy Long Denied
chapters.summary: In the archive, Elodie identifies the dead man as Tobias Fenwick, beneficiary of a claim she helped deny seven years ago. His file lists one witness to his near-drowning: Maren Quill, certified dead since 1998. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the first vertigo of a case that predates him.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Won't Weep
chapters.summary: Elodie interviews Fenwick's widow, Ivy, who grieves with suspicious precision and mentions the clothes 'looked better on him.' A locked boathouse on her property hums with a generator. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the hunter's thrill of a first real thread.

chapters.title: Dead Women Don't Sign Leases
chapters.summary: Elodie traces Maren Quill's death certificate and finds it signed by a doctor who died before the date on the document. Someone manufactured a death — carefully, expensively. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: cold clarity hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: Bellwether Lane After Dark
chapters.summary: Elodie walks the lane at night and is followed by a figure who knows the tide schedule better than he does. He loses them in the churchyard, but finds a fresh footprint in salt mud beside Fenwick's old family plot. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the investigator becoming the investigated.

chapters.title: The Saltmere Inheritance
chapters.summary: A retired solicitor, over brandy, sketches the founding family's estate: a fortune held in trust, payable only if all heirs survive to a fixed date. One heir's death would redirect everything. Fenwick's death reopens the trust. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the case acquiring a motive with teeth.

chapters.title: What the Tide Took
chapters.summary: The police drag the flats and recover Fenwick's satchel — containing a photograph of Maren Quill, alive, dated three weeks ago. Elodie realizes the witness everyone swears is dead has been watching him. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: fear braided with a strange, unwelcome hope.

chapters.title: Ivy's Ledger
chapters.summary: Elodie breaks into the boathouse and finds Ivy's meticulous ledger of payments — hush money flowing to half the village for twenty years, entries stopping the week of Fenwick's death. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of a whole town complicit.

chapters.title: The Man Who Hung
chapters.summary: Elodie interviews the brother of a gardener hanged in 1998 for a murder on Bellwether Lane — the murder that made Maren Quill a 'corpse.' The brother insists the gardener died protecting someone. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: grief as evidence; duty beginning to war with conscience.

chapters.title: A Meeting on the Marsh Road
chapters.summary: A note in Elodie's own handwriting — which he never wrote — lures him to the marsh road at dusk. He glimpses Maren Quill: alive, weathered, unrepentant, and gone before he can speak. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the case turning intimate and uncanny.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: Elodie matches the forged note and the forged death certificate to one hand — and finds the same handwriting in Ivy Fenwick's old letters. The widow has been writing Maren's death for decades. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: triumph soured by the question of why.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Through parish records and a schoolteacher's memory, Elodie reconstructs Maren's hidden life: the fake drowning, the years in the marsh cottage, the payments that kept her ghost alive. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: reluctant admiration for a woman who chose erasure.

chapters.title: The Denial
chapters.summary: Elodie confronts his own role: the insurance denial that pushed Fenwick toward desperation and into someone's scheme. He drafts a resignation letter he doesn't send. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the price of survival includes the survivor's guilt.

chapters.title: Second Body on the Flats
chapters.summary: The schoolteacher who talked is found drowned, dressed in Fenwick's clothes. The pattern is now unmistakable: someone is staging deaths as messages. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: dread — the killer is performing for an audience of one.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Waited
chapters.summary: Elodie identifies the trust's contingent beneficiary: Ivy Fenwick, who married into the family and has waited twenty years for the inheritance that Maren's survival keeps suspended. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the motive snapping into focus like a lock turning.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Elodie discovers Maren and Fenwick were lovers; his death was an accident she witnessed and could not report without surrendering her ghost-life. Ivy learned Maren lived — and began killing to bury the witness for good. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the case becoming a tragedy, not a puzzle.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Maren contacts Elodie directly: she will surrender, testify, and resurrect herself — if he can guarantee the gardener's name is cleared first. Elodie must decide whether the law deserves the truth it will use. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: duty and love pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Ivy, tipped off, moves to kill Maren before the tide turns. Elodie races the flooding marsh to reach the cottage first, finding it empty, a lamp still burning. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: terror stripped to its simplest form — running out of time.

chapters.title: The Verdict of Bellwether Lane
chapters.summary: At the old gallows field on Bellwether Lane, Ivy holds Maren at the water's edge, demanding she die as the record says she did. Elodie arrives and offers the trade: the trust's confession for Maren's life. Ivy falters as the tide takes her footing. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the climax — truth as the only currency left.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: The flats give up what they took: Ivy's confession, recorded, and the gardener's hidden letters proving his innocence. Ivy is arrested; the trust dissolves into restitution. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: grim, exhausted justice.

chapters.title: Resurrection Papers
chapters.summary: Maren signs her own death certificate's reversal with a shaking hand, choosing a small, difficult life over a safe ghost's one. Elodie testifies to the gardener's posthumous pardon. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: the quiet cost and grace of survival.

chapters.title: What the Investigator Keeps
chapters.summary: Elodie closes the file he swore never to open again and keeps one thing: the photograph of Maren alive, as a reminder that some verdicts are meant to be overturned. He walks Bellwether Lane at dawn as the tide recedes. POV: Elodie. Emotional beat: resolution — peace earned, not given.
